subject: Clarifying Redwood's default log horizon and deletion path for requests/outputs
messages:

Subject: Default retention clarifications (prompts vs outputs / EU residency)

Hi Vivek —

Quick follow from our S&T review: can you confirm what Redwood stores by default for hosted API requests? Specifically: 1) are raw customer prompts retained longer than generated outputs, 2) what triggers deletion (customer API delete vs automatic TTL), and 3) how residency is applied for EU customers when using the hosted service? We want short, concrete examples we can show the ops team.

Also, do you have a one-page diagram that shows where requests live over time?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Default retention clarifications (prompts vs outputs / EU residency)

Hi Oliver —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers first, then a couple of illustrative examples below. Attaching a quick diagram and our SOC2 evidence guide.

Summary:
- What we store by default: request metadata and model inputs (prompts) are captured for diagnostics; generated outputs are also captured by default for quality monitoring and evals.
- Retention & deletion triggers: we apply a default TTL of 45 days for most hosted API logs. Deletion occurs automatically when TTL expires; customers can also request immediate deletion for specific records via the API or by opening a support ticket (we validate account ownership).
- Residency: for EU-region customers, data ingested into an EU labeled project is stored in EU-resident storage. Cross-region backups are minimized; any cross-region replication requires an explicit customer opt-in or is only used for disaster recovery under strict controls.

Illustrative scenarios:
1) Developer sends 3 prompts during a session (sessionID=abc123). By default: prompts + token-level metadata stored for 45 days, outputs also captured for 45 days. If the developer calls the DELETE API for sessionID=abc123, we mark records for immediate purge and schedule erasure within 48 hours (subject to legal holds).

2) EU pilot: Customer creates an EU project and uses hosted API in eu-west-1. All request/response artifacts are written to EU buckets and follow the 45-day TTL. Logs required for billing (aggregated usage totals) are retained for 365 days in the EU; raw prompt/output blobs remain under the 45-day window unless customer requests extended retention.

Notes & exceptions:
- Prompts that match included CSM/bug reports may be pulled into longer-term storage if the customer consents.
- Attachments (file uploads) are treated as generated artifacts and follow the same TTL unless stored in a customer-managed bucket.
- Legal holds / compliance export requests will pause automatic deletion; we surface this in the retention API.

Next steps: happy to jump on a 30-min call with your ops/security folks to walk the diagram.

Best,
Vivek
VP, Product — Redwood Inference

Oliver —

Adding legal / controls nuance:
- Deletion requests: we authenticate against the account owner and capture an audit record of the request (the audit trail is retained longer for compliance; that audit entry does not include raw prompt/output blobs).
- Residual derivatives: when we generate fingerprints or anonymized telemetry derived from prompts (e.g., hashed n-gram stats used for model quality), those derivatives may be kept beyond the 45-day window but are non-reversible and are stored as aggregated telemetry.
- Contracting: if BrightBank requires strict non-replication outside the EU, we can include language in the contract and provision a Private deployment or EU-only Dedicated capacity.

Uploading the SOC2 guide and a retention-diagram for your ops team (see attachments).

Hi Oliver —

Thanks — quick operational clarifications from the delivery side so your ops folks have the exact endpoints:
- API delete endpoint: POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/data/delete with payload {"keys": [...]} — typical SLA for processing deletes is 48 hours; we send a status callback to the account admin webhook.
- Export for audits: we produce a time-limited export link (signed URL) for requested artifacts; exports are logged.
- Billing records: aggregated usage records are retained for accounting for 12 months and are exportable via the console.

If you're free next Tuesday we can run a 20-min demo of the delete flow and show the EU project config.

Cheers,
Marissa
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
